title: No saxophones in old bands; joining the Eureka band around 1934
summary: Old bands used clarinet, alto and baritone, not saxophones. Clark joined the Eureka band about 1934, playing trombone, in an eleven-man line-up.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Did they use saxophones in those old bands?

They used clarinet. See they used the clarinet and the alto and the baritone. You see the alto gives you a compliment just like a banjo do in an orchestra. And we call it the peck horn. Because he just makes the same note mostly all the time. Now and then he'll change his note. See what I mean? Yeah I know the part. You see that's the way, that's the set up. But the fellas don't want to play that instrument. Now when I came into the Eureka band we had E flat clarinet, alto and baritone. I was playing trombone then. We had three cornets and two drums. Used to use eleven men. When did you join the Eureka? Well I joined the Eureka about 1934.
You weren't one of the founders then?

No I'm not a founder. But it hadn't been organized very long when I joined. But I remember when it was organized. Because I was playing in a concert band at that time. It says a man here by the name of Henry Pritchett. He set up a concert band of thirty pieces. Still here? Oh he's still here. Yes. But I mean he don't fool with any bands anymore because he's pretty foreign age now.
